newsitem.title: CHINA: HK-Shanghai cooperation will top competition - Tung.
newsitem.headline: HK-Shanghai cooperation will top competition - Tung.

text.p: Hong Kong and Shanghai enjoy a range of opportunities to cooperate due to China's rapid economic development despite being locked in competition, Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa said on Wednesday.

Tung was visiting his birthplace of Shanghai for the first time since being chosen to head the Hong Kong Special Administrative Zone following the handover of the British colony to China at midnight on June 30.
"There will be some competition (between Hong Kong and Shanghai) but the area for cooperation is much wider," he told a news conference held to mark a seminar on Hong Kong-China economic ties.

"If China continues to develop as it is now developing -- and I fully expect it to continue to develop this way -- China will need a number of Shanghai's and Hong Kong's, because in 50 years' time, China's economy will be the biggest in the world," he said.
Tung said China's rapid economic growth provided huge opportunities for Hong Kong business, adding: "The opportunities will be even more numerous after the handover."

"The competition that we will see between us is the competition of mutual encouragement and joint development, there should not be any question of one replacing the other," he said in a luncheon speech earlier.

The chairman of the Hong Kong Trade Development Council (HKTDC), Victor Fung, said Hong Kong was looking to cooperate with Shanghai to take joint advantage of the opportunities presented by China's economic development.
"Hong Kong is focusing on working together with Shanghai enterprises in other parts of the country," Fung said.
The message from other participants at the seminar, organised by the HKTDC, was much the same -- China is big enough to allow both Hong Kong and Shanghai to continue to grow and prosper.

Zheng Bolin, deputy chief of the Bank of China's Hong Kong-Macau management office, told the seminar the fear of Shanghai replacing Hong Kong as an international financial centre was understandable but unjustified.

"Shanghai at this point is a long way behind Hong Kong in many areas. I believe that in the short term, at least before the renminbi (Chinese yuan) becomes freely convertible, Shanghai cannot become an international financial centre," Zheng said.
But he said that by the time Shanghai was ready to take on such a role, "the huge scale of the Chinese economy will be perfectly capable of supporting two financial centres."
"At that time, Hong Kong will still have its own advantages, both cities will have their special characteristics. The question of one replacing the other does not exist," he added.

Tung, who was scheduled to return to Hong Kong on Wednesday afternoon, will fly to Beijing on Thursday with Hong Kong's senior civil servant, Chief Secretary Anson Chan, for meetings with top Chinese leaders.
